title: Spring: dry friction or damping? Fifteen seconds would tell
description: A glider on a track between two springs, filmed for 15 s with nothing of known size in view. Dry (sliding) friction forecasts the held-out motion best (8.8% against 10.9% for viscous damping), but the two laws are only 4 BIC apart, so neither is confirmed. Both give the same natural frequency, 2.740 ± 0.002 rad/s, which needs no scale. The agent asks for the same pull filmed for 15 s, where the laws separate by 33 times the tracking noise.
